newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Santos sold down on rights issue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Santos sold down on rights issue.

text.p: Shares in oil and gas producer and explorer Santos Ltd were sold down 22 cents or about four percent in active early trade on Wednesday after announcing a one for eight rights issue and an asset purchase.

But brokers said the initial reaction had been overdone and positive underlying sentiment had helped boost Santos' share price back up off its A$4.68 low to be only 14 cents down at A$4.76 at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
"It's a fairly typical kneejerk reaction to a rights issue," said Ord Minnett director of institutions Eric Gale.
"It may be a little bit overdone. Santos is a long way from being overvalued," Gale said.

Earlier, Santos announced it would acquire a 30 percent stake in the East Spar oil and gas field off the Western Australian coast from WMC Ltd for A$181 million. It also said it planned to raise about A$270 million through a one-for-eight rights issue at A$4.00 a share.

Santos said the renounceable rights offering would help fund its major expansion programme, while maintaining the company's financial gearing at a sound level. The issue has been fully underwritten by E.L. & C. Baillieu Ltd and J.B. Were & Son.
Other brokers also said Santos' share price was likely to weather the immediate sell-down because of what they said was its strong exploration portfolio.
"We like how they're driving into exploration," said one broker, who saw value in Santos' share price over A$6.00.
"People are just seeing right now they're going to have to shell out for the rights issue, which will soak up their demand for further Santos shares," the broker said.
